sources_considered.why: Dated primary release record establishes that GPT-5.5 followed the post.
Independent government testing directly compares GPT-5.5 and Mythos Preview.
The dated index confirms April 30, 2026 publication of the cited evaluation.
Independent government account dates GLM-5.3's release and evaluates its cyber capabilities.
Direct comparison with Mythos Preview supplies a second rival example. Anthropic's competitive interest is disclosed.
The announcement alone would not establish comparable capability; stronger primary release and comparative evaluation records were found.

evidence_items.explanation: The release record establishes public availability of a competing model after Marcus's post. Comparable cybersecurity capability is established separately by AISI's evaluation.

evidence_items.locator: Cyber Task Results, following the Expert-level comparison
evidence_items.explanation: AISI publicly reported comparable cyber performance: GPT-5.5 scored 71.4% on its Expert tasks against Mythos Preview's 68.6%, with overlapping uncertainty. These controlled capability tests support similarity, while AISI cautions that they do not establish success against well-defended real targets or ordinary public-user access to those capabilities.

evidence_items.publisher: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation
evidence_items.locator: Opening paragraph; capability qualifications in key findings
evidence_items.explanation: NIST establishes the later release of a second developer's model and documents advanced vulnerability-discovery and exploitation results. It also finds GLM-5.3 below the then-current US frontier, which limits claims of universal parity but does not exclude similarity to April's Mythos Preview.

evidence_items.locator: GLM-5.3 can develop working exploits end to end, ExploitBench paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's published comparison reports 50 successful exploit attempts for GLM-5.3 against 56 for Mythos Preview under the same ExploitBench evaluation. This corroborates the emergence of a second similar rival, although the evaluator develops the competing Mythos model.
